packed.verdict: Revision 6 resolves most of the r5 must-fix list in substance, and the accepted item-1 design (reachability gates in V0(d), a ratio-plus-resolvability V0(b), absolute L2 bars kept for step 0.4 only) is written in coherently across Part 2, V0, Part 8.2 and Part 9. All 26 Part 11 sha256 values match their files. The fixed stage2_oc.py reproduces stage2_oc_output.txt byte for byte (e521d8a9...), and every joint, conditional and unconditional figure quoted at lines 696-712 and in Part 8.7 matches that output. The edits do introduce a few new defects, though. Most serious: the new 4.5b literal slope-3 identity rule contradicts the two places where the protocol runs an identity check in a slope-1.5 world: 4.8's known-answer 'identity residual <= 1e-6' on the frozen central-quartile cells, and step 0.4's 'stall_slope 1.5 (identity check only)' world. As written, both would fail by construction and end the step INCOMPLETE. 4.5b's world list also omits step 0.3's slope-1.5 replays. Second: the new 4.8 q1/twin_min reproduction sets a tolerance of '1e-6' without saying absolute or relative. Saved q1 reaches 496 in float32 (1 ULP = 3.05e-5), so read as absolute it demands bit-exact replay and invites a spurious INCOMPLETE. Third: the reachability gates handle item 5's tolerance inconsistently. K1c's gate adds 0.15; K1a's adds nothing. V0(d) reachability, as a V0 item, also turns an observed K1 pass into INCONCLUSIVE. Fourth: V0(b)'s floor drops to 0.20, which shrinks the absolute allowance to 0.08 and adds an undisclosed noise-driven path to INCONCLUSIVE. The remaining items are wording and specification slips, including one leftover 'within this step's cap'. None of these creates a false-PASS path; every one either fails closed or costs power. One more text pass is needed before A1. No new design choice is required from the user.

verified.claim: The reachability gates treat item 5's predictor tolerance inconsistently. K1c's gate is rho_hat_C(s10) >= 0.65, justified as 'the bar plus item 5's 0.15 tolerance', which assumes KC tracks the true rho while rho_hat may overstate it. K1a's gate, rho_hat_C(s05) >= 0.5 + 0.4 x rho_hat_R(s05), adds no 0.10 s05 tolerance. Under K1c's own logic, a correct, smooth critic can therefore still FAIL K1a by up to 0.10, which is exactly the misleading FAIL the gate exists to prevent. Under the stated model 'KC is about rho_hat' (:199), K1c's gate should instead be 0.5. Separately, 'rho_C >= rho_R (both >= 0.83) is sufficient' is slightly wrong: 0.6 x 0.83 = 0.498 < 0.5. The condition needs rho_C >= 5/6 and puts no lower bound on rho_R.
verified.evidence: Example: median rho_hat_R(s05) = 0.125 and median rho_hat_C(s05) = 0.55 pass the K1a gate (0.55 >= 0.55). Item 5 allows true rho_C = 0.45, so worst-case K1a is about 0.45 - 0.05 = 0.40 < 0.5. That gives a FAIL, and reading 2 attaches if KC_R <= 0.1 x rho_hat. DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:204 versus :201.
verified.fix: Choose one model and apply it to both gates. Either K1a: rho_hat_C(s05) >= 0.6 + 0.4 x rho_hat_R(s05) and K1c: 0.65 (KC tracks rho), or K1a as written and K1c: 0.5 (KC tracks rho_hat). Mirror the choice in V0(d), Part 8.2 and Part 9 row 1. Replace 'both >= 0.83' with 'rho_C >= rho_R and rho_C >= 5/6'.

check.reason: Confirmed. Item 5 (:184) bounds |min_k P_k - Q_nostall|, so rho_hat - rho lies within ±0.10 at s05 and ±0.15 at s10. K1c's gate (:204, :617) adds the 0.15 tolerance, which treats KC as tracking true rho. K1a's gate (:201, :617) adds no 0.10 tolerance, which treats KC as tracking rho_hat, and :199 states the rho_hat model. The two reachability gates in V0(d) therefore rest on different error models. Under K1c's model, a correct, smooth CUTOFF critic whose rho_hat_C overstates rho_C by 0.10 can pass the K1a gate and still miss K1a, which is the misleading FAIL the gate exists to prevent. The :203 caveat covers only the anchor-set mismatch, not predictor bias. The sufficiency clause is also slightly wrong: rho_C >= rho_R gives rho_C - 0.4 rho_R >= 0.6 rho_C, so it needs rho_C >= 5/6, and 0.6 x 0.83 = 0.498 < 0.5. It needs no lower bound on rho_R. Either fix the suggestion offers restores coherence; mirror it in Part 8.2 and Part 9 row 1.

verified.section: V0(d) reachability (:616-617) versus label precedence (:458-465) and Part 2 (:197)
verified.claim: Reachability sits inside V0, and INCONCLUSIVE outranks FAIL and PASS. A seed where a K1 criterion is 'not reachable' therefore voids the whole Stage 1 result even when K1a/K1c actually passed: for example, a critic whose over-valuation exceeds the smooth-extrapolation prediction. Part 2 and V0(d) describe the gate as turning a would-be FAIL into INCONCLUSIVE ('declared INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL'). Its effect on an observed pass is never stated. KC is measured against true Q^pi, so an observed KC >= 0.5 is real over-valuation whatever rho_hat is. Discarding it costs power without adding validity.
verified.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:197 ('A criterion that a correct, smoothly extrapolating critic could not pass is declared INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL'); :617; precedence table :458-465; decision rules apply 'in every seed' (:599).
verified.fix: Either apply reachability per criterion only to a miss (K1x fails and is not reachable in a seed: INCONCLUSIVE; a pass stands), or state explicitly that non-reachability voids an observed K1 pass, give the reason, and add that to Part 8.2.

check.reason: Refuted. V0(d) is a validity precondition that is checked whatever the outcome, and the label precedence (:458-465) states without ambiguity that INCONCLUSIVE outranks PASS, so the effect on an observed pass is defined. Part 8.2 (:789-791) already says unconditionally that if the gate fails, 'V0(d) makes Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE', and it discloses the cost: 'a good learner can end the line of work without an answer'. :197 ('INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL') does not claim a pass would stand. The r5 option (a) the user accepted was specified as 'INCONCLUSIVE otherwise'. The proposed change, applying the gate only to misses, would make the precondition depend on the outcome. That is an asymmetric, forking-path design, and voiding a pass whatever the outcome is the defensible choice. When rho_hat is small, an absolute KC_s10 >= 0.5 can also reflect generic approximation error rather than the hidden knee. This is consistent, disclosed and implemented coherently.

verified.section: V0(b) resolvability floor and ratio clause (:609-610); Part 8.2 (:786-791)
verified.claim: Lowering the floor from 0.85 to 0.20 shrinks the absolute allowance |median KC_s05(RANDOM)| <= 0.4 x rho_hat_R from at least 0.34 to as little as 0.08. The 0.4 coefficient was sized for multiplicative, scale-invariant kink rounding (:207). Additive critic-approximation noise in KC is not scale-invariant, so a correctly labelled, competent RANDOM learner with rho_hat_R of about 0.2-0.3 can fail the ratio clause on noise alone. Part 8.2 lists only reasons (i) and (ii) for a V0(b) INCONCLUSIVE, and its 'competent learners' bullet mentions only V0(d).

verified.fix: Disclose a reason (iii) in Part 8.2: a competent RANDOM learner with small rho_R can fail the ratio clause through absolute KC noise. Optionally add an additive allowance c (|KC_R| <= 0.4 rho_hat_R + c), carry it into the K1a reachability gate (0.5 + 0.4 rho_hat_R + c), and report the absolute |KC15_s05| scale from step 0.3's onset contrast.

check.reason: Partly confirmed. r6 lowers V0(b)'s floor from 0.85 to 0.20 (:609), so the absolute allowance 0.4 x rho_hat_R can shrink from >= 0.34 to 0.08. The 0.4 coefficient is justified only by scale-invariant kink rounding (:207-208). No additive KC noise floor is measured anywhere. The cited MAE of 19-23 is an offset error that mostly cancels over a 0.05 action difference, so it overstates the noise. Part 8.2 (:786-791) lists only reasons (i) and (ii) for a V0(b) INCONCLUSIVE, and its competent-learner bullet mentions V0(d) only. So the new risk that a competent RANDOM learner with small rho_R fails the ratio clause on additive KC noise is undisclosed. The risk is fairly unlikely, since rho_R near 0.2 implies |Q| of about 27 at E2 by the 0.0075|Q| scaling. It costs power, not validity: the result is INCONCLUSIVE and can never be a false PASS. Disclosing it as reason (iii) is the minimal fix; an additive allowance is optional.

packed.verdict: Revision 6 is not ready for A1. It is one short text pass away, and no script or data work is needed. The user's choice (reachability gates in V0(d) instead of absolute rho floors) is the right shape. As written, though, it does not deliver its stated promise that a criterion a correct critic could not pass ends INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL, in either direction. (1) V0(d) is an unconditional V0 item, and INCONCLUSIVE outranks both FAIL and PASS (5.0, :458-465). So when K1a is unreachable in one seed, Stage 1 is labelled INCONCLUSIVE even if K1a actually passes, or K1c fails clearly (reading 1), or K2/K3 fail. That throws away informative outcomes. (2) The reachability statistic differs from K1a's statistic: it is a difference of medians, not the median of paired differences, and its anchor sets are not specified. Its tolerance treatment also disagrees with K1c's. So K1a can still FAIL in a case where it could not have passed. (3) 4.5b's 'literal identity' rule contradicts step 0.4's slope-1.5 identity check, so implementing it as written forces an INCOMPLETE. Smaller issues: V0(b)'s claim to cover softplus widths of 0.04-0.05 is stale now that the large floor is gone. Step 0.4's item-1 median dropped to 0.75, below the 0.834 that K1a reachability needs under equal continuations. 4.5b should name the float64 states field and the full no-stall physics dict. The stage2_oc.py fix is correct: rerunning it from a scratch copy gives byte-identical output, every quoted joint figure matches, and P(R3|R1) at -1.5 is unchanged. All 26 Part 11 hashes verify, and the thrust reconstruction in 4.5b is implementable exactly from the canonical B matrix.

low_findings.claim: K1a and K1c reachability treat predictor tolerance inconsistently, and the sufficiency statement has an arithmetic slip.
low_findings.evidence: :199 asserts KC ~ rho_hat. Under that model K1c is reachable at median rho_hat_C(s10) >= 0.5, yet :204 adds item 5's 0.15 tolerance (0.65). Under the alternative model KC ~ rho, with rho_hat up to 0.10 above rho at s05, K1a would need 0.6 + 0.4 x rho_hat_R, but :616 uses 0.5. In that model a K1a FAIL is possible where it could not pass, for example rho_hat_C = 0.5 + 0.4 rho_hat_R with rho_C = rho_hat_C - 0.10. Also :202 says 'rho_C >= rho_R (both >= 0.83) is sufficient'. At rho_C = rho_R = 0.83 the condition needs 0.5 + 0.4 x 0.83 = 0.832 > 0.83, so it fails. The correct statement is rho_C >= rho_R and rho_C >= 5/6 (0.834). rho_R needs no lower bound.
low_findings.fix: Pick one model and apply it to both. Either use KC ~ rho_hat with thresholds 0.5 + 0.4 rho_hat_R and 0.5, or add the tolerance to both: 0.6 + 0.4 rho_hat_R and 0.65. Correct :202 to 'rho_C >= rho_R and rho_C >= 0.834'.

verified.section: Stage 1 V0(d) (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:614-618); 5.0 label precedence (:458-465); Part 2 (:197); Part 8.2 (:789-791)
verified.claim: The reachability gate is unconditional, and because INCONCLUSIVE outranks PASS and FAIL it masks valid outcomes. The design says 'INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL', but the rule as written gives 'INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS or FAIL'. Unreachability of one criterion also masks every other criterion.
verified.evidence: V0(d) is listed among the V0 (INCONCLUSIVE) items with no condition on K1's outcome (:616-617). Labels take the first that applies, with INCONCLUSIVE above FAIL and PASS (:458-465). Consequences, per seed: (i) if KC_s05(C) - KC_s05(R) >= 0.5 although median rho_hat_C(s05) < 0.5 + 0.4 x median rho_hat_R(s05), a valid K1a PASS (a critic over-valuing beyond the smooth model) becomes INCONCLUSIVE; (ii) if K1a is unreachable while K1c is reachable and fails in every seed, reading 1 (:647), the protocol's main negative finding, is lost; (iii) failures of K2 (actor does not enter), K3a/K3b/K3c, which do not depend on rho, are relabelled INCONCLUSIVE. Part 2 :197 says the gate applies to 'a criterion that a correct ... critic could not pass', which is a per-criterion, on-failure rule; the V0 implementation is neither.
verified.fix: Make reachability per criterion and per seed, applied only when that criterion fails. If K1a (or K1c) fails in seed i and its reachability condition fails in seed i, record that criterion as 'not testable (unreachable)' in seed i. The step is INCONCLUSIVE only if no other criterion fails validly. Otherwise the remaining FAIL readings apply, with the untestable criterion's reading suppressed. A criterion that passes stands whatever its reachability. Remove reachability from the V0 list, or keep it as V0 only in this conditional form, and update Part 2 :197 and Part 8.2 to match.

check.reason: Confirmed. DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:616-617 puts the combined 'K1 is reachable' condition (K1a AND K1c) inside V0(d) with no condition on how K1 came out. Under the precedence table (:458-465) INCONCLUSIVE outranks both FAIL and PASS. This has three effects. (i) K1a unreachable while K1c is reachable and fails in every seed: reading 1 (:647) is valid but gets masked. (ii) A K1a/K1c pass that exceeds the smooth-model bound becomes INCONCLUSIVE. (iii) Failures of K2 and K3a-c, which do not depend on rho, are relabelled. The per-seed recording rule (:456) keeps the raw outcomes but attaches no label and no reading. The design rationale at :197 and :617 ('INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL', 'could not pass it') is a per-criterion rule that applies on failure, so the V0 wording overshoots what the accepted design choice intends. Fixing this does not reverse the user's accepted choice; it only makes the gate conditional and per criterion.

verified.section: V0(d) K1a reachability (:616) vs K1a (:624); Part 2 Link to Stage 1 (:200-203); V0(c) (:613)
verified.claim: The K1a reachability statistic does not match K1a's statistic, and its anchor sets are undefined. So K1a can still FAIL where a smoothly extrapolating CUTOFF critic plus a worst-allowed RANDOM critic could not have passed.
verified.evidence: K1a is the median over common gated anchors of the per-anchor difference [KC_s05(C) - KC_s05(R)] (:624). The gate is a difference of medians, median rho_hat_C - 0.4 x median rho_hat_R (:616), with no anchor set stated for either median. rho_hat is only meaningful on predictor-valid anchors (:185). V0(b) takes rho_hat_R on the RANDOM-predictor-valid subset (:610). No set or floor is defined for anchors predictor-valid under CUTOFF's continuation, and V0(c) (:613) floors only the common set and the RANDOM-valid set. Counterexample with 3 anchors: rho_C = [1, 1, 0], rho_R = [2, 0, 0]. The gate gives 1 - 0.4 x 0 = 1 >= 0.5, so it passes. With KC_C,i = rho_C,i and worst-case KC_R,i = 0.4 rho_R,i, the per-anchor differences are [0.2, 1, 0], median 0.2 < 0.5, so K1a FAILs by construction. Part 2 :203 admits the set mismatch makes the worst case 'approximate', but the condition is now a gate that decides between INCONCLUSIVE and FAIL, so approximate is not good enough.
verified.fix: Define reachability with K1a's own form, on one named set: reach_K1a(i) = median over anchors that are common-gated AND predictor-valid under both continuations of [rho_hat_C,j - 0.4 rho_hat_R,j] >= 0.5. A more efficient alternative replaces 0.4 rho_hat_R,j with the observed KC_s05(RANDOM)_j, since V0 already uses RANDOM's KC. Add that both-valid set to V0(c) with a floor of 32. State that K1c's reachability median (rho_hat_C(s10)) is taken on the CUTOFF-predictor-valid common anchors.

check.reason: Partly refuted. The anchor set is not undefined: :601 says 'K1a, K1c and V0 all use [the common gated anchors]', so V0(d)'s medians default to the common gated set. That set still includes up to 10% predictor-invalid anchors, which a median largely tolerates. The mismatch in form is real: the gate uses a difference of medians (:616), while K1a uses the median of per-anchor differences (:624). The 3-anchor counterexample is arithmetically valid and satisfies V0(b), since median KC_R = 0 <= 0.4 x 0. In it the gate passes, K1a fails by construction, and reading 2's guard (:648, median KC_R <= 0.1 rho_hat) does not block the misreading. Part 2 :203 admits this is only approximate. The impact is limited to K1a FAIL readings and needs anchor-level anticorrelation between rho_C and rho_R; K1c's gate has a consistent form. The fix (a per-anchor form on the both-predictor-valid set) is cheap, but the effect on validity is second-order.

verified.section: 4.5b Literal identity (:369) vs step 0.4 worlds (:548-549) and label table (:557); 4.5 (:358)
verified.claim: The new rule that the identity test uses the literal slope-3 formula and 'never physics.stall_slope' contradicts step 0.4. Step 0.4 runs the L2.1 identity in a stall_slope-1.5 world ('identity check only') and forces 'the T-image of each W slot in each stall world'. With T3 hard-coded, the 1.5 world fails the identity by construction, which triggers INCOMPLETE.

In the 1.5 world the true thrust is T1.5 (canonical thrusterchain.py thrust(), lines 205-210 region; docstring line 17), so Q(s, a) differs from Q(s, T3(a0)) - 0.3(a0^2 - T3^2) by O(0.1-1). 4.5b's own synthetic fixture (:370) relies on exactly this failure.
verified.fix: Use per-world literal constants. Hard-code T3 (slope 3.0) for the stall world and T1.5 (slope 1.5) for the identity-only world, and assert each against the physics dict recorded in that receipt, so a mix-up still breaks the identity. Reword :369 to say 'the literal Part 0 formula for the stall world, and a literal slope-1.5 formula for step 0.4's identity-only world, never read from physics.stall_slope'.

check.reason: Confirmed, and wider than stated. :369 hard-codes T3 ('never physics.stall_slope') for 'the L2.1 identity test'. Step 0.4 runs a slope-1.5 world tagged 'identity check only' (:367, :548), and forced a0 includes 'the T-image of each W slot in each stall world' (:549). With T3 hard-coded, that world's identity residual is O(0.1-1), far above 1e-6, which is INCOMPLETE under :557. A second conflict: step 0.3's known-answer reproduction on the frozen central-quartile cells requires 'identity residual <= 1e-6' (:430). Those cells come from the stall_slope 1.5 world (:501, 'T15 ... which is what these critics were trained on'; canonical default stall_slope 1.5 at thrusterchain.py:116,143). So the literal-T3 rule makes step 0.3 INCOMPLETE by construction as well. The fix is literal constants per world, each asserted against that receipt's physics dict, covering step 0.3's cells too.

verified.section: V0(b) ratio clause and resolvability floor (:609-610); Part 2 coverage note (:205-208); Part 8.2(ii) (:788)
verified.claim: Without the large floor, V0(b)'s claim to cover kink rounding up to softplus width 0.04-0.05 no longer holds at the rho scales the protocol now expects. The resolvability floor's anchor set is also unspecified.
verified.evidence: Item 5 allows |rho_hat - rho| <= 0.10 at s05, so the worst case is rho = rho_hat_R + 0.10. A correctly labelled critic with KC/rho = r passes only if r <= 0.4 rho_hat_R / (rho_hat_R + 0.10). That ratio is 0.267 at the floor of 0.20 (covers width ~0.02), 0.333 at 0.5 (~0.035), 0.343 at 0.6 (~0.035), 0.358 at the old 0.85 floor and 0.364 at 1.0. :206 says the ratio 'does not depend on ... the scale of rho', which is true for KC/rho but not for the gated KC/rho_hat. :207 notes the predictor-bias dependence, but Part 8.2(ii) still says 0.04-0.05. Part 2 :195 itself expects learner-scale rho of about 0.6-0.7, where coverage is about 0.035. Separately, the floor clause (:609) names no anchor set, while the ratio clause (:610) uses the predictor-valid subset.
verified.fix: Either make the allowance use the upper end of the predictor tolerance, |median KC_s05(R)| <= 0.4 x (median rho_hat_R(s05) + 0.10), which restores width ~0.05 coverage at every scale. Or keep 0.4 x rho_hat_R and disclose in Part 2 and 8.2(ii) that coverage falls to about width 0.02-0.035 for rho_hat_R between 0.2 and 0.6. In either case, state that the 0.20 floor is evaluated on the RANDOM-predictor-valid subset, the same set as the ratio.

check.reason: The anchor-set half is refuted. :602 says 'V0(b) further restricts them to anchors that are predictor-valid under RANDOM's own clipped continuation' as a general statement for V0(b), so the 0.20 floor is on the same subset as the ratio. The coverage arithmetic is correct: worst case r <= 0.4 rho_hat/(rho_hat+0.10), which is 0.267 at 0.20 and 0.333 at 0.5. Against the stated KC/rho table (0.25/0.31/0.35 at widths 0.02/0.03/0.04), that is about width 0.035 at learner-scale rho, not 0.04-0.05. Part 2 :207 already discloses that coverage depends on predictor bias, but 8.2(ii) (:788-789) still states 0.04-0.05 without qualification. Lowering the floor from 0.85 to 0.20 in revision 6 makes this worse. The consequence is only a higher chance of a false INCONCLUSIVE, which the protocol already discloses, not an invalid FAIL or PASS. So this is a disclosure inaccuracy, low severity.

critic.verdict:
Revision 6 is not ready for A1. It needs one more text-only pass. No new data, screens or user design choice are required.

What r6 got right: it resolves most of the r5 list in substance, and the accepted item-1 design is written in coherently. That design removes the absolute rho floor from V0(b) and keeps a ratio clause with a 0.20 resolvability floor. It gates K1 reachability in V0(d), keeps the absolute L2 bars for step 0.4 only, and discloses the cost in Part 8.2. Both lenses independently confirmed four things. All 26 Part 11 hashes match. The fixed stage2_oc.py reproduces its saved output byte for byte. Every Stage 2 figure quoted in the text matches that output. The 4.5b thrust reconstruction is well posed.

Why it is not ready:
1. Gate-logic defect (high). The new 4.5b 'literal identity' rule hard-codes slope 3 and says 'never physics.stall_slope'. It therefore fails by construction on the two identity checks that run at slope 1.5: the 4.8 known-answer check on the frozen central-quartile cells (trained at 1.5) and step 0.4's '1.5 identity check only' world. Step 0.3, the first executed step, would come out INCOMPLETE.
2. Inconsistent reachability gates (medium). The two gates assume different predictor-error models. K1c adds item 5's 0.15 tolerance and K1a adds none. As a result, a smooth critic can still FAIL K1a by up to 0.10, which is exactly the outcome the gate exists to prevent. The 'both >= 0.83' sufficiency line is also arithmetically wrong.
3. Unstated tolerance (medium). The 4.8 q1/twin_min reproduction gives '1e-6' without saying absolute or relative. Read as absolute, it is below one float32 ULP at |q| of about 500, so it effectively demands bit-exact replay of a sealed known-answer check.

I adjudicated the one conflict between the lenses (R6-1 against N4) toward the accepted design. V0(d) stays an unconditional, outcome-independent validity precondition. The text must say plainly that it also voids an observed K1 pass and masks K2/K3. It must not be rewritten into an apply-only-on-failure rule. Everything else is wording or specification, and none of it opens a false-PASS path.

Separately, ':202 rho_C >= rho_R (both >= 0.83) is sufficient' is wrong: at 0.83 the condition needs 0.832. V0(b)'s ratio clause tolerates less kink rounding than the text claims at the expected rho scales (about softplus width 0.02-0.035, not 0.05). The reachability arithmetic is a worst-case model built on medians and item 5's tolerance bands. Anchor-level correlations between the two arms' gaps can still make it approximate unless the per-anchor form is adopted.

Sealed numerical tolerances (known-answer reproduction, thrust reconstruction, identity residual) combine with the second-failure-is-INCONCLUSIVE rule. Any tolerance stated too tightly or ambiguously can end a step on float32 or GPU numerics rather than on the science.

The world-certification safeguards (literal per-world identity formulas, physics-dict assertions, float64 reconstruction) are only as strong as their exact wording. A slope mix-up is caught only if each receipt names its world's literal formula and full dict.
